messages:
mike: Heads-up — we need to lock acceptance gates for the upcoming on‑prem + VPC private deployment PRD. Customer A just asked for a firm list of "must-have" networking behaviors before we sign the SOW.
anya: Thanks. I sketched a draft acceptance checklist this morning. Pasting the core items so we can iterate.
kevin: Can you drop it here? I'll check for gaps vs. the current infra constraints.
lucy: quick note: try to keep the initial set conservative — we want a smooth first rollout.
anya: Sure. Draft: 1) Customer-managed egress: customer supplies either a static IP pool or NAT gateway; our control plane must accept a declared egress IP set and validate routes. 2) BGP handoff optional: support bgp session for advanced customers; fallback to static route if not configured. 3) CIDR collisions: reject overlaps with customer's primary VPC; provide precise error + remediation steps. 4) TLS termination: we terminate mTLS on their LB only if they opt-in; otherwise our side handles TLS to the node. 5) Audit logs: per-request audit to Kinesis/S3 for 90 days by default, option for longer retention. 6) KMS/HSM: keys must be customer-provided for private, with rotation window >= 30d. 7) Network policy: explicit firewall rules doc, default deny. 8) Health checks: active probe via customer VPC to confirm path and NAT behavior.
kevin: Nice. Missing: asymmetric routing detection, and a graceful fallback when customer egress becomes unreachable. Add: 9) Asymmetric route detection with alert and auto-failover. 10) Fallback: automatic switch to Redwood-hosted fallback model with notify + traffic cap.
taylor: Also we need acceptance tests for MTU differences and TCP MSS issues — lots of customers have weird appliances that mess with large payloads.
jordan: +1 on MTU. Add a step in the test plan: upload ~1MB payloads and confirm streaming tokens don't break.
mike: Good. Can we map these to specific PRD acceptance criteria? e.g., what constitutes "pass" for the BGP handoff?
anya: Proposal: BGP pass = (a) session established, (b) 7 days of stable routes in staging with <0.1% BGP flap, (c) synthetic trace shows <50ms added RTT from control plane. If any fail, we mark as blocked.
lucy: That sounds reasonable. For the fallback, what's the SLA implication? We should avoid promising auto-failover for customers on Dedicated contracts without confirming payment scope.
kevin: Action: add a matrix in PRD mapping customer tier -> allowed fallback behaviors. I'll own that. @kevin: action item.
anya: I'll own test harness and docs for the egress validation tool. @anya: action item.
taylor: I'll create a short test suite for MTU/MSS/TCP fragmentation and run it against the staging onprem stack.
jordan: I'll coordinate with infra to reserve a lab with a simulated NAT device and one with BGP-capable router.
mike: deploy-bot: start ci/net-tests with job id net-onprem-1974
deploy-bot: Job net-onprem-1974 queued. Estimated time: 35m.
anya: Edge cases to call out in PRD section "Known limitations": - Multi-tenant customers that use overlapping /24 pools — we will require per-tenant routing isolation for GA. - Customers with carrier-grade NAT that rewrite source ports unpredictably — our connection tracking heuristics may misattribute sessions. - If customer rotates KMS keys outside agreed window, logs will show encryption errors but state remains until rekey.
kevin: Good to surface. Also call out the port exhaustion case when customers NAT thousands of short-lived connections; we should document recommended ephemerals and connection pooling.
lucy: For launch criteria, propose: 1) All critical acceptance tests pass in staging for 3 consecutive days. 2) 2 pilot customers completed end-to-end onboarding with minimal operator intervention. 3) Rollback playbook validated. 4) Oncall runbook published + tabletop done.
anmike: Typo — small rename: change bullet 2 -> "at least one pilot customer on production-like network".
mike: Sorry, that's me — renaming as requested.
kevin: Timeline? If we start pilots next week, I'd say 4 weeks to pilot completion assuming no major infra blockers.
taylor: Does the PRD include instrumentation requirements? We need per-request token latency histograms and per-route error codes.
anya: Yes — add: metric set: request_latency_p50/95/99, token_emit_rate, egress_fail_count, bgp_flap_count, mtufailure_count.
jordan: For rollout, include canary percentages: 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 72h windows with monitoring checks and auto-rollback on >3x baseline error rate.
lucy: Quick decision: do we require customers to sign a network readiness checklist before GA? I'm leaning yes.
mike: Yes — one-page signoff that customers confirm firewall rules, NAT behavior, and KMS access.
kevin: I'll draft the checklist and drop it in the PRD doc tomorrow.
anya: ok, I'll update the RFC with acceptance criteria + test plan. Putting a link placeholder: https://redwood.internal/prd/onprem-networking (will replace with real link).
taylor: I'll add the MTU test scripts under infra repo and reference them.
jordan: tagging infra: @infra-team please confirm availability for lab next Tue/Wed.
infra-team: available slots Tue morning and Wed afternoon.
mike: last thing — edge-case negotiation with legal: some customers want full control over egress IPs but also want Redwood to handle failover. We need legal to sign off on risk. @lucy can you loop legal?
lucy: will do, looping legal now.
mike: OK, thanks all. Next sync: PRD review tomorrow 10:00am. :thumbsup:
